text: Hi, I'm Paul. Butler is an Alexa+ add-on that acts for you, and turns your corrections into rules the AI can't break.
This is our open-source simulator, connected to the live stack on AWS. The Black Box on the right records every gateway decision.
I don't give Butler commands. I tell it what's happening.
Tell Butler six friends from the dinner crew are coming over Friday at seven.
type: Tell Butler six friends from the dinner crew are coming over Friday at 7.

text: It makes a plan and gets started.
Butler never interrupts. It waits until I ask.
How's Friday looking?
One decision is mine, so I'll tap it.
That tap runs under a separate approval identity, not the AI.
Every action has a receipt.
Why did you buy the drinks?
What it used, what it turned down, and the rule that allowed it.
Don't buy drinks without asking me.
Yes.
The AI only picks a rule template. Plain code turns it into a Cedar policy in AgentCore. Now it's live at the gateway.
I'm travelling Thursday to Sunday. My parents are staying at the house.
Butler tried to buy drinks for my parents. The gateway denied it, outside the model, before anything was bought.
Anything you need from me?
So instead of buying, it asks.
What did you do this week that I might disagree with?
Butler runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Thanks for watching!
